body:
Follow-on noticed while building Enix tracker task 01M3J8W21 (Enix-side RAISE/PRESENT hooks for "is this already ruled?" -- a PreToolUse hook on mcp__trk__decision + Bash `trk decision`, and a UserPromptSubmit hook on Scott's "what's a decision to rule in <arc>" phrasing, both backed by a TF-IDF retrieval engine over docs/DECISIONS.md + trk list --decision --all --json + ruling-shaped design-doc paragraphs).

Those Enix-side hooks already cover both moments the task's acceptance criteria named, and the retrieval script is already usable manually from Enix's own checkout (python3 .claude/hooks/decision-rule-check.py match "<question>"). A trk-side `decision-check <id|question>` verb would mainly help an interactive ad hoc check run OUTSIDE a hook context -- e.g. before filing via the bare CLI in a terminal with no Claude-Code hook attached, or from a different consuming repo. Moderate value, not essential, since the real leak point (an agent raising/presenting a fork) is already caught.

Reported per Enix task 01M3J8W21's fence: "a trk decision-check verb would live in the sibling repo, do not build it in Enix; if judged needed, file it as a follow-on". Not filed as urgent -- judge independently whether it is worth building, and whether it should be per-repo (reading that repo's own DECISIONS.md/design docs) or something trk ships generically.

DROPPED 2026-10-02 (Scott agreed): not trk's to build. The generic manual check already exists: trk list --decision --all <terms> searches every decision's title, body and tags, ruled ones included. The valuable part, ranking over a repo's own DECISIONS.md and design-doc paragraphs that read like rulings, would read files outside .tracker/ and impose a docs layout. That is the 'trk greps its consumers' direction ruled out in 01M1FMNSZ. The leak point (an agent raising or presenting a fork) is already covered by the Enix hooks; the bare-terminal case can run that repo's script or list --decision.
